policy: A route-scoped selector is scoped to a value a page writes: html[data-wingman-route="<key>"] takes the WingmanRouteKey members routeCatalog.ts declares (plus the literal AppShell writes for the admin page), and .wm-route-<segment> takes route-manifest.json segments (plus the admin literal the shell adds for the same page). The two vocabularies are separate, and the difference is the point: 14 of 29 routes have a kebab-cased segment that is not a key and a camelCase key that is not a segment, so data-wingman-route="call-coach" matches nothing even though call-coach is a live segment, and .wm-route-callCoach matches nothing even though callCoach is a live key. This file lists the dead values the tree keeps today, each with the count of rules that name it and the story that left it behind. The count is pinned, so a pinned scope that spreads to more rules has to be read again; an entry whose rules are gone has to come down; and a value with no entry fails. It is a delegation of a cleanup, never a way to pass a gate that just went red: adding a value here is a decision about dead styling, and the gate names the file and a selector for every value it reports.

The rules behind it are dead styling a person has not deleted yet: pinning them keeps this gate honest about what is dead while refusing to admit a new scope, and the entry fails the moment the rules are removed.
